Looping you both in — forwarding Acme's redlines. Key point: they want to carve IP indemnity out from the overall liability cap (i.e., IP indemnity damages not subject to cap).

Rishi — can legal propose tight language that limits exposure but addresses their ask? Options we discussed internally:
1) Full carve-out: "Notwithstanding any cap on liability, Redwood's liability and obligations arising from claims of third-party intellectual property infringement, including defense, settlement and indemnity, shall not be subject to such cap."
2) Limited carve-out: carve out IP indemnity but cap consequential and exemplary damages; require claims to be promptly notified and allow Redwood to control defense/settlement.
3) Escrow/insurance approach: keep cap but require Redwood to maintain specific IP insurance and/or a restitution escrow for certain claims.

Timeline: Acme needs sign-off by May 1. Please suggest proposed redline text and any recommended commercial mitigations (insurance limits, notice/defense mechanics).

Thanks — Vanessa
VP, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Vanessa / Lauren —

See proposed compromise language below. It is designed to be narrow (limits runaway exposure), preserves our ability to avoid admitting liability, and keeps the customer comfortable. We should attach this as a redline in the order form.

Proposed language (suggested for Order Form / MSA):
"Notwithstanding any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, Redwood's liability and indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims alleging infringement of patents, copyrights, trademarks, or trade secrets arising from Redwood-provided models or services ("IP Claims") shall be subject to the following: (a) Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold Customer harmless from and against any damages finally awarded against Customer by a court of competent jurisdiction arising from such IP Claims; (b) Redwood's indemnity obligation shall not be limited by any monetary cap in this Agreement for amounts actually and finally awarded to Customer for such IP Claims; provided, however, that Redwood's aggregate liability for indemnity and defense costs arising from any single IP Claim shall not exceed Redwood's insurer-approved policy limits for such claim where applicable; and (c) Customer shall (i) provide prompt written notice of any claim; (ii) allow Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim; and (iii) reasonably cooperate in the defense."

We can offer the following commercial mitigations to Acme:
- Add requirement that Redwood maintain Commercial General Liability and Technology E&O coverage with a minimum IP endorsement (we can commit to x/yr limits — R&D to confirm).
- If customer insists on unlimited exposure, propose a hybrid: carve-out from cap except for punitive/exemplary damages and excepting claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer modifications.
- Offer an escrow reserve for amounts above the cap for a limited period while claims are litigated.

Lauren: any redline tweaks? Also note this language ties to defense/control which buyers often want reversed; we should keep control.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: John Spencer <john.spencer@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Acme Legal Ops <legal@acmecorp.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form (redlines attached) — Redwood proposed language

John —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear timeline. We reviewed internally with legal and commercial. Below is Redwood's proposed compromise to include in the order form; we believe it addresses Acme's protection needs while limiting open-ended exposure:

--- Proposed insert (redline attached as proposed_cap_language.txt) ---
"Notwithstanding any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, Redwood's indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims alleging infringement of intellectual property rights arising from the provision of Redwood's services shall not be subject to the monetary cap set forth in this Agreement, except that (i) Redwood's aggregate liability for indemnity and defense costs arising from any single IP Claim shall be limited to Redwood's applicable insurance coverage limits for such claim where Redwood's insurer has agreed in writing to provide coverage; and (ii) Redwood shall have the right to assume sole control of the defense and any settlement negotiations for such claim; provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim that would impose an admission of liability or obligation on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)."

Commercial mitigations we are offering:
- Redwood will maintain IP liability/Technology E&O coverage; we will share certificate of insurance and allow evidence of coverage as reasonably requested.
- Carve-out language excludes claims that arise solely from Customer content, Customer modifications, or Customer's breach of law or misuse.

Attachments: proposed_cap_language.txt (text) — redline snippet included.

If Acme is comfortable with that, we can update the order form and route to DocuSign by end of week.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
